sentences.text:
That on 01.09.2023 at about 09.30 PM., the petitioner was driving the vehicle bearing Reg No.KA-53- EW-1157 in Old madras road, near K.R.Puram, Govt College,
wherein the driver of the vehicle bearing Reg No.KA-01-JW-0604 drove it, in a high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner and caused accident.
In the accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

He took first aid at K.R.Puram Govt Hospital, later he was shifted to Shir.Laxmi hopsital wherein he took treatment as an inpatient for the accidental injuries and he has spent Rs.2,00,000/-
for his medical treatment.
3. Petitioner stated that he is 23 years of age working as a courier incharge at Blue Dart company and was earning Rs.24,000/- per month,

Further he stated that the accident has occurred due the negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle and the jurisdictional police have registered Cr.No.300/2023 against the driver of the offending vehicle.

He alleged that the Respondent no.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle and insured his vehicle with respondent no.1 and accident caused due to the sole negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and as such both are liable to pay the compensation with interest and he prayer this tribunal to award the compensation amount by allowing the petition.
4.

After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondents, respondent no.1 appeared and filed the power and written statement by denying the petition averments and contended that insured has violated the policy conditions.
Respondent no.2 has not choose to contest the petition and he placed ex-party.
5. Petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and examined doctor as PW.2 produced and marked 14 documents which are at Ex.P.1 to 14 and they are fully cross examined.
6. Respondent no.1 examined its legal managed as RW-1 and produced Ex.D1 and she is fully cross examined.
7. I have heard the arguments from the counsel appearing for the petitioner, counsel appearing for respondent No.1 has filed written arguments.
I have perused the same along with entire records.

Counsel appearing for respondent No.1 has relied on the following authorities:
1. MFA No.6154/2019 (MV-D/- Hon'ble High court of Karnataka order dated 14.12.2023)
2. MFA No.3297/2019 (MV-D- Hon'ble high court of Karnataka order dated 13.04.2023)
8.

On the basis of pleadings, my learned predecessor in office has framed the following :

College, wherein the driver of vehicle bearing Reg No.KA- 01-JW-0604 drove it in high speed and rash and negligent manner and dashed against the two wheeler and caused the accident and there by petitioner sustained grievous injuries as alleged in the petition.?

2.Whether respondent no.1 proves that the insured has violated the policy condition and petitioner sustained injuries due to self fall as as contended in the written statement.?
3.Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation? if so, what is the quantum and from whom?
4.What order or award?
9. After carefully going through the evidence placed on record and taking into consideration of facts and attending circumstances of the case, my findings to the above issues are as follows;
Issue no.1: In the affirmative Issue no.2: In the Negative Issue no.3: In partly affirmative Issue no.4:
As per final order for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1 to 3 :- I have taken these issues together for common discussion so as to avoid the repetition of facts and reasoning.
PW.1 being the petitioner, he reiterated the petition averments in his examination-in-chief affidavit.
Petitioner has tender the police records, that is C/copy of FIR, complaint, police intimation,
mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate, Final report which are at Ex.P.1 to 4, 6 to 8.

Petitioner has tendered his DL as per Ex.P.12.
11.
On careful perusal of the aforesaid documents it is evident that one Sandeep Kumar S/o Bayatappa was the driver of the offending vehicle.

The final report filed by the investigating officer which is at Ex.P8, IMV is at Ex.P6, the aforesaid documents establishes the involvement of the offending vehicle, rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The final report which is at Ex.P8 is filed after investigation and it is the prima facie proof of the accident and the involvement of the offending vehicle and rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly the police records cannot be doubted and disbelieved.
Respondent No.1 has fails to establishes his conditions that insured has violated the policy conditions.
In the cross examination of DW-1, he admit that final report is filed against the driver of the offending vehicle.
It is true that petitioner has tendered his valid DL as per Ex.P12.

sentences.text: Petitioner has tender the wound certificate, discharge summary which are at Ex.P.7 & 8, the entry therein shows that the petitioner sustained grievous injury that is left distal radius fracture and ORIF with plating fixation was done to him by way of surgery on 01.09.2023 and he took treatment for the accidental injuries as an inpatient for 3 days in Sri.Laxmi Hospital and he has spent Rs.22,544/- as per Ex.P.10.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the compensation under the following heads.

13. Pecuniary damages (Medical expenses) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization,
Medicines, Transportation, Nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure:
14. Petitioner took treatment at Sri.Laxmi Hospital as an inpatient for 3 days, for the grievous injuries and left distal radius fracture.
Admittedly petitioner has taken treatment and under went surgery for attendant charges, transportation, nourishing food, he might have spend some more expenses.
Therefore I award Rs.20,000/- in addition to actual medical expenses Rs.22,544/- as per Ex.P.10.
Petitioner is entitled for Rs.42,544/-under this head.
Loss of income during laid up period.
15. The petitioner has not substantiated his nature of work and income as alleged in the petition.
Accident took place on 01.09.2023, however as per notional income chart, the notional income for the year 2023 is Rs.16,000/-, and same is assessed and considered as his monthly income.
Considering the accidental injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, I am of view that at-least one month he has lost his income.

Therefore I award Rs.16,000/- X 1 month = Rs.16,000/-
as compensation under this head.
Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
16. The petitioner has examined the as PW-2.
He deposed that, petitioner has 12% of whole body disability.
Learned advocate for the respondent argued that the assessment of PW-2 is on higher side.
I have perused the evidence of PW-2 wound certificate, discharge summary given by the hospital, X-ray etc.
Evidently petitioner has not examined the doctor who have treated him in the hospital.
It is true that petitioner sustained grievous injury that is left distal radius fracture and ORIF with plating fixation was done to him by way of surgery on 01.09.2023.
It is true that PW-2 has admitted that fracture is united and petitioner can perform his work from his right hand effectively and there is no difficulty for him to walk and sit.
The percentage of loss of earning capacity due to accidental injuries is different from the percentage of physical disability due to accidental injuries.
Considering the medical reports and oral testimony of doctor, the whole body disability of the petitioner is assessed as 9%.

The notional monthly income of the petitioner is assessed as Rs.16,000/-, the age of petitioner as on the date of accident is 23 years as per the entry in Aadhar card, DL which are at Ex P.11 and 12 .
The multiplier applicable to this case is "18".

Therefore loss of income on account of permanent disability is calculated as follows; Rs.16,000/-(Monthly income) X 12 (Months) X 18 ( Multiplier)
X9% (Functional Disability) = Rs.3,11,040/- Hence, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.3,11,040/- as Ajay Kumar R vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199366707/

sentences.text: (IV)Damages for pain and sufferings and loss of amenities:
17. It is undisputed fact that petitioner has sustained grievous injury.
During the hospitalization and rehabilitation period, he might have undergone lot of pain and sufferings.
There fore I award Rs.10,000/- under these conventional heads.

V) Loss of Amenities :-
18.
The petitioner has to forego certain amenities available for him.

Therefore I award Rs.10,000/-
as compensation under this head.
19. Except these heads the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under any other heads.

In all the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:

TOTAL Rs.3,89,584/-
20.
Rate of Interest:

The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in Sarala Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, wherein it is held that it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a.

sentences.text: Accordingly I award the interest at the rate of 6% P.A on the compensation amount form the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
21. Liability:

The insurance company has not disputed the validity of the policy of the offending vehicle, on the other hand, respondent No.1 has failed to prove the contention as contended in his written statement.

In the authorities relied on by the counsel appearing for respondent No.1,
wherein liability is fastened on the owner of the offending vehicle, for the reason that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having the valid DL as on the date of the accident.

In the present case,
as per the final report, accused No.1 was the driver of the offending vehicle as on the date of the accident and he was not charge sheeted for not having the valid DL as on the date of the incident.

Accordingly Respondent No.1 is the liable to pay the compensation amount and respondent No.1 is directed to deposit compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within one month from the date of this order.

Hence with the aforesaid discussion based on the evidence placed on record,

22. Issue No.4; For the foregoing reason and discussion, on point No.1, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor vehicle Act,1988, is partly allowed with cost.
Petitioner is entitled for the compensation amount of Rs.3,89,584/- with interest at the rate of 6% P.A from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
Respondent no.1 is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this tribunal with in 30 days from the date of the judgment.

After depositing the compensation amount with interest, shirestedar is directed to release entire compensation amount with interest in favour of the petitioner through K2, after compliance of mandate of circular No.39/2020 dated 17.01.2020.
Advocate fee of Rs.1000/- is fixed.
All the interim applications pending if any stands disposed of.
Draw award accordingly.
